profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed to Prime, most likely Prime Data Centers given the California and Texas registry locations. Prime Data Centers own site states the company was established in 2017 in California and is now headquartered at 400 North Ervay Street, Dallas, Texas, under founder and CEO Nicholas Laag, and describes itself as majority founder owned. The company reports 28 data centers across 13 campuses globally with a 4 plus gigawatt expansion pipeline, and lists Silicon Valley and Dallas among its confirmed North America markets, alongside Austin, Chicago, Los Angeles, Phoenix, and Sacramento, matching both states where this registry lists a Prime facility. No building specific address, opening date, or individual MW figures for this particular registry row were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
Prime DFW01-01 publishes 20 MW of IT capacity across 213,000 square feet of technical space in Dallas, ranking sixth among Texas facilities with disclosed power figures.

At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, this facility supports roughly 500 racks. At 10 kW per rack, typical for mixed enterprise and GPU colocation, it supports around 2,000 racks. The operator has not stated which density the facility targets, so both are estimates rather than confirmed specifications. The power-to-space ratio of 94 watts per square foot suggests a mixed-use colocation design rather than a purpose-built high-density AI training hall, though the operator has not confirmed this.

SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO 27001 certifications indicate the facility meets independently audited security and information management standards. These qualifications matter for tenants with data-handling compliance requirements or international security obligations. No tenant names are published.

Across Texas, 133 facilities have been mapped on this site, but only 13 publish capacity figures. Those 13 account for 389 MW of disclosed IT capacity, making Prime DFW01-01's 20 MW roughly 5 percent of that known total. The remaining 120 mapped facilities publish no capacity data, so the state's actual total is unknown and likely higher than 389 MW. Any statewide grid constraint analysis depends on closing this disclosure gap.
